GameAnalytics explained: What's free, what's Pro, and what each feature does
GameAnalytics
Last updated: Oct 14, 2026
min read
A breakdown of every GameAnalytics product, pricing, and how each feature maps to a real studio need.
The GameAnalytics platform is built as an IQ Suite: three distinct products that cover player analytics, market intelligence, and data infrastructure. Each product serves a distinct purpose, targets a different buyer, and has its own free-and-paid tier split. Studios can start on the free tier at any scale and add Pro capabilities product by product as they grow.
This post walks through every feature in AnalyticsIQ, MarketIQ, and PipelineIQ, with a short explanation of what each one does for a game studio. If you're evaluating GameAnalytics against another tool, or trying to figure out whether the free tier covers what you need, this is the complete picture.
A note on scale: AnalyticsIQ and MarketIQ have genuine free tiers with no MAU caps, no credit card required, but PipelineIQ is Pro-only because it's designed for teams with specific data infrastructure needs,
AnalyticsIQ
AnalyticsIQ
is the player behavior analytics tool at the heart of the
platform
. It tracks what players do inside your game, how they engage over time, and what that behavior means for retention, monetization, and overall growth. It's used by over 100,000 indies, studios, and publishers across mobile, Roblox, PC, console, and VR, and the core capabilities are free at any scale.
Free in AnalyticsIQ
The free tier is built to give any studio a complete picture of player behavior without needing a Pro upgrade. It includes:
Pre-defined dashboards
that surface your game’s key health metrics the moment you integrate the SDK, no setup required.
Custom dashboards
built to show the exact view your team cares about, no SQL and no config files.
Event tracking
with game-specific event types (business, resource, design, progression, ad) built for how studios actually think about data.
Offline events
so player activity still lands in your data even when the device has no connection.
Live event debugging
to verify event implementation in real time instead of guessing whether your tracking works.
Funnels
that show exactly where players drop out of your onboarding, levels, or monetization flows.
Real-time monitoring
of your game’s live metrics as they happen, so you catch issues before players do.
Cohorts
grouping players by behavior or attributes, with each cohort’s evolution tracked over time.
Retention
measured on day 1, 7, 30, or any custom window that matters to you.
Matrix visualization
to see multi-dimensional data in one view and spot patterns a single chart would miss.
Error tracking
that catches crashes and errors in your live game before they become one-star reviews.
A/B Testing
for running controlled experiments on any part of your game and measuring what actually moves the metric.
Remote Configs
to change game parameters in real time without shipping a new build.
Player Segments
grouped by behavior or attributes, usable across analytics, experiments, and content targeting.
AI Agent (free tier)
that answers natural-language questions about your game’s data instantly, with 3 messages per user per day.
For most indie studios and early-stage teams, this covers the full analytics workflow. The ability to run A/B tests, segment players, measure retention, and get AI-assisted analysis without paying anything is unusual for an analytics platform at this depth.
AnalyticsIQ Realtime
AnalyticsIQ Pro
AnalyticsIQ Pro
starts at $49 per month, or roughly $29 per month billed annually with the 40% yearly discount, and unlocks deeper visibility and automation for teams that need more than the free tier can offer. It adds:
Health monitoring
that catches technical issues like FPS drops, memory leaks, or slow app boot times before they silently hurt retention and show up in your reviews.
Distributions
showing how metrics are spread across your player base, instead of leaving you to rely on misleading averages.
Hourly granularity
to zoom into intraday patterns during launches, LiveOps events, or incident response.
